introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2020. Duration: two and a half hours. Do ALL the tasks (Task 1, Task 2 and Task 3) specified in the question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two and Group Three. Each version has three tasks: Task 1 (word processing, 20 marks), Task 2 (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task 3 (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks).

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (the pictures 'foxandstork' and 'hareandtortoise' found on the desktop) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**GROUP THREE - TASK 1 (20 marks)**

*The text in Figure 1 is a career letter to a friend.*

> Mojoali Brenda  
> P.O. Box 10000  
> Old Town, Limbe  
> Fako Division  
> SW Region  
> 20th June 2015 *(these six address lines are at the right of the page)*
>
> Dear Crispin,
>
> I want to write to you about my future career. I am a school-leaver and this year I am finishing school. When you leave school, you understand that the time to choose your future profession has come. It is not an easy task to choose the right job for you.
>
> There are a lot of different professions and it is really hard to choose the one, which would be interesting for you and will help you earn your living. Generally, I think that choosing the right job is the main question not only for a school-leaver, but also for all the family.
>
> I would like to become a teacher. In my opinion, to be a teacher is not an easy task because you need not only to love children, but you also should have an ability to explain things clearly, know your subject profoundly and be an all-around person. Though this is not the easiest task, I am sure that I have got almost all necessary qualities to become a really good teacher.
>
> Nowadays it is very important to know a foreign language, especially English. More and more people need qualified teachers to teach them today. I understand that this profession is greatly demanded and that is why I would like to become an English teacher.
>
> I wait for the letter with impatience.  
> Best wishes,  
> Brenda
>
> **Figure 1**
incertitudes: Le PDF (15 pages, scan sans couche texte) contient TROIS versions du même sujet pratique : « Group One » (pages 1 à 5, livret 2xxx/0595/3B/Grp 1), « Group Two » (pages 6 à 10, Grp 2) et « Group Three » (pages 11 à 15, Grp 3), chacune avec Task 1 (traitement de texte, 20 points), Task 2 (tableur, 20 points) et Task 3 (programme C ou Pascal, 10 points). Transcrites en neuf fichiers : numero_exercice G1-T1, G1-T2, G1-T3, G2-T1, ..., G3-T3 ; groupes ["GROUP 1"], ["GROUP 2"] ou ["GROUP 3"]. Rien n'est imprimé sur le fait qu'un candidat ne traite qu'une seule version : regles_choix reste vide (convention des Paper 3 de pratique).

Les filigranes gcerevision.com / Kawlo, les cadres d'en-tête (numero de centre, nom du candidat, « For examiners' use only »), les lignes à compléter, la réponse manuscrite « Microsoft office Word 2007 » portée à la main sur la page 2 et les artefacts de scanner sont ignores. Les images « foxandstork » et « hareandtortoise » et les fichiers du bureau ne figurent pas dans le PDF.

Aucun logiciel (Word, Excel, compilateur C ou Pascal) n'a été exécuté : les menus et les étapes sont donnés de mémoire (Office récent) et ne sont pas testés. Les formules de tableur ont été traduites en Python et exécutées sur les données du sujet (COUNT, COUNTA, ROUND, AVERAGE, RANK, COUNTIF). Le code C et Pascal n'a pas été compilé : sa logique a été vérifiée par une simulation Python fidèle (mêmes entrées, mêmes sorties, cas limites).
Aucun corrigé officiel n'existe : les réponses sont rédigées. Les répartitions de points dans les corrigés (quand il y en a) sont indicatives ; les points imprimés du sujet ne sont jamais modifiés.

Task 1, Group Three : points imprimés (1+1+8+1+2) + (1+1) + (1+3) + 1 = 20 ; l'item 3c (couleur « Brick red ») n'a pas de point imprimé et la mention « (3 mark) » (au singulier) est celle du sujet. Le texte de la Figure 1 est recopié tel qu'imprimé, y compris « all-around » et « one, which » ; les lignes de l'adresse sont à droite de la page. La couleur « light sky blue » est donnée en RVB 135, 206, 250 (couleur nommée light sky blue) et « Brick red » par une valeur indicative : aucune valeur n'est imposée par le sujet. « Text background colour » est lu comme un ombrage du texte (pas la couleur de page).

questions.enonce_markdown: Launch any word processor program installed in your PC and: a) Set paper size to A4.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Start the word processor and open a blank document. *Layout* tab > **Size** > **A4** (21 cm x 29.7 cm).

questions.enonce_markdown: b) Set left and right page margins to 0.75 inches (or 2cm) respectively.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: *Layout* tab > **Margins** > **Custom Margins...**. In the *Margins* box set **Left** and **Right** to **0.75"** (or 2 cm) and click *OK*. (0.75 inch is 1.9 cm, so the two values given in the question are practically the same.)

questions.enonce_markdown: c) Type the text of Figure 1.  *[8 marks]*
d) Change the text background colour to a light sky blue colour.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the whole text (*Ctrl + A*). In the *Home* tab open the arrow of **Shading** (paint bucket) and choose a light sky blue (*More Colors...* > *Custom*, for example Red 135, Green 206, Blue 250, the colour named light sky blue). The background behind the text becomes light blue.

questions.enonce_markdown: e) Add a page border of width 3pt.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: *Design* tab > **Page Borders**. In the *Borders and Shading* window, *Page Border* tab, choose the setting **Box**, set **Width** to **3 pt**, check that *Apply to* is **Whole document**, and click *OK*. A 3 pt frame now surrounds every page.

questions.enonce_markdown: Bold the address section of the letter.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the six address lines (from *Mojoali Brenda* to *20th June 2015*) and click **B** (Bold, *Ctrl + B*).

questions.enonce_markdown: Set the line spacing of the whole letter to 1.5.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the whole letter (*Ctrl + A*), open **Line and Paragraph Spacing** in the *Home* tab and choose **1.5**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Add a custom diagonal watermark text with the following specifications: a) Font Size: 100 points  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: *Design* tab > **Watermark** > **Custom Watermark...** > choose **Text watermark**. In the **Size** box choose **100** (not *Auto*), and keep **Layout: Diagonal**.

In the same *Printed Watermark* window, type **Career Letter** in the *Text* box (capital C and L, a space between the two words), then click *Apply* and *OK*. The words appear in large letters across the page, running diagonally behind the letter.

In the *Color* box of the same window choose a brick red: a dark red from the palette, or *More Colors...* > *Custom* with a reddish-brown value such as Red 178, Green 34, Blue 34. The watermark is then printed in that colour. (No mark is printed for this item; the colour is part of the 3 marks of the watermark.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Save your work as Task 1 in your work directory.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: *File* > **Save As** > working directory, file name **Task 1**, then *Save*.
*File* > **Print** (*Ctrl + P*), 1 copy, then *Print*; attach the copy to the booklet.
